_note: Country knowledge for the investigator: where to look, which buyer protections apply and what to check. These are LEADS to verify, not facts to state; every claim in a report still needs its own source. Keyed by ISO country code. October 2026.

IN.name: India
languages: and the state's language (for example Marathi, Tamil, Kannada)
sources: The state RERA portal: registration certificate, promoter, filed completion date and extensions, quarterly progress, complaints and orders (Maharashtra: MahaRERA)
MCA21: the promoter company's master data, directors, charges and filing history
IBBI: insolvency proceedings against the promoter or its group
eCourts and Indian Kanoon: civil suits, consumer cases and orders naming the promoter or project
BSE and NSE filings when the group is listed: results, auditor qualifications, pledges, guarantees, tax actions
The state registration department (IGR): registered sale transactions and encumbrances
protections: RERA section 13: no more than 10% advance before a registered agreement for sale
RERA section 18: interest for delayed possession, or withdrawal with refund and interest
RERA section 14(3): five years' liability for structural and workmanship defects after handover
RERA section 4(2)(l)(D): 70% of buyer money kept in a separate project account
checks: The registered promoter versus the brand it is sold under
Every extension of the completion date and whether allottees consented
Commencement and occupation certificates for the buyer's building and floor
Charges on the land or receivables and lender consent to sell
A 30-year title search

GB.name: United Kingdom
sources: Companies House: the selling company, its officers, charges and filing history
HM Land Registry: title, charges and price paid for nearby new homes
The local planning authority's portal: permissions, conditions and section 106 obligations
The Building Safety Regulator: gateway approvals for higher-risk buildings (18 metres or seven storeys)
The Gazette: insolvency notices
The New Homes Quality Board register and the government's Responsible Actors Scheme list
protections: The New Homes Quality Code and the New Homes Ombudsman, where the developer is registered
A ten-year structural warranty (for example NHBC or Premier)
The Leasehold Reform (Ground Rent) Act 2022: ground rent on new long leases limited to a peppercorn
The Building Safety Act 2022 gateways before work and before occupation
checks: The company that signs the contract versus the brand
The long-stop date and the right to rescind
Where the deposit is held
Service charges, estate charges and any heat network
Outstanding planning conditions for the buyer's building

AE.name: United Arab Emirates (Dubai)
sources: The Dubai Land Department (DLD) and its Dubai REST app: project registration, escrow account, completion percentage
The Real Estate Regulatory Agency (RERA): project status and the service-charge index
Oqood: off-plan sale registration
Dubai Pulse open data: transactions
Dubai Financial Market disclosures when the developer is listed
protections: Law 8 of 2007: buyer payments go into the project's escrow account
Law 13 of 2008 as amended by Law 19 of 2017: what a developer may keep if a buyer defaults, by percentage of completion
checks: The seller on the sale and purchase agreement versus the brand or master developer
The escrow account against the DLD record
Whether instalments follow certified progress or dates
Default, assignment and delay clauses
Service charges

CA.name: Canada
sources: Ontario: the HCRA Ontario Builder Directory for the builder's and vendor's licence, conditions, convictions and charges
Ontario: Tarion for warranty coverage, claims and conciliation history
Ontario: the land registry (OnLand) and the Ontario Business Registry
British Columbia: BC Housing's licensed residential builder registry and the developer's disclosure statement
Municipal building permits and court records (CanLII)
protections: Ontario: Tarion's new home warranty, deposit protection and compensation for delayed closing or occupancy
Ontario condominiums: a ten-day cooling-off period after signing or receiving the disclosure statement (Condominium Act, 1998)
British Columbia: the disclosure statement and rescission period under the Real Estate Development Marketing Act
checks: The vendor's and builder's licences and any conditions or convictions
Tentative and firm closing dates and the delay compensation
How deposits are held and insured
Interim occupancy fees, development-charge caps and termination (sunset) clauses
HST and any rebate assignment

MY.name: Malaysia
sources: The housing ministry's (KPKT) TEDUH portal: the developer's licence and the project's advertising and sales permit
SSM (Companies Commission): the developer company's profile, directors and charges
KPKT's list of delayed, sick and abandoned private housing projects
The local authority: the certificate of completion and compliance (CCC)
The land office or the state's land department: title, strata title status and encumbrances
Bursa Malaysia disclosures when the developer is listed
protections: The Housing Development (Control and Licensing) Act 1966: licensed developers and statutory sale agreements (Schedule G for landed, Schedule H for strata homes)
Liquidated damages for late delivery under the statutory agreements
The Housing Development Account: buyer payments held for the project
The Tribunal for Homebuyer Claims for disputes with the developer
checks: The licence and the advertising and sales permit are valid for this project
The developer's record on KPKT's delayed and abandoned list
Delivery of vacant possession and the liquidated damages clause
Strata title status and the timeline to transfer
Maintenance charges and the sinking fund

US.name: United States (pilot: Florida and New York)
sources: SEC EDGAR: filings by listed builders, including risk factors and litigation
Federal court dockets (PACER, CourtListener) and state court records
Florida: Sunbiz for the selling company, the Division of Florida Condominiums filings, county official records and the property appraiser
New York: the Attorney General's offering-plan filings for condominiums, ACRIS recorded documents and NYC Department of Buildings permits and violations
County and city building permits and code violations
protections: Florida condominiums: the buyer's cancellation right after signing a developer sale contract, and deposits held in escrow (Florida Statutes chapter 718)
Florida condominiums: milestone structural inspections and structural integrity reserve studies
New York: the offering plan and its amendments, and deposits held in escrow
checks: The selling entity (often a single-purpose LLC) and who stands behind it
The offering plan or prospectus and every amendment
The escrow agent and the outside completion date
Association budget, reserves and any special assessments
Construction-defect litigation against the builder

DE.name: Germany
sources: The common register portal (Handelsregister): the developer company (Bauträger), its directors and filings
Official insolvency notices (insolvenzbekanntmachungen.de)
Published annual accounts (Unternehmensregister and Bundesanzeiger)
The local building authority: the building permit (Baugenehmigung)
The land register (Grundbuch): access needs a legitimate interest, usually through the notary
protections: The Makler- und Bauträgerverordnung (MaBV): payments only as construction stages are completed, or against a bank guarantee
A developer contract (Bauträgervertrag) must be notarised
A priority notice (Auflassungsvormerkung) in the land register before any payment
Five years' liability for construction defects under the Civil Code
checks: The developer's trade licence under section 34c of the Trade Regulation Act
The priority notice and the financing bank's release letter (Freistellungserklärung)
The payment schedule against the MaBV stages
The handover and acceptance (Abnahme) terms
Insolvency notices for the developer and its group

NL.name: Netherlands
sources: The KvK company register: the developer, its directors and filings
The central insolvency register
Woningborg and SWK: whether the home is covered by a new-home guarantee and warranty
The municipality: the environmental and building permit
The Kadaster land registry: title and mortgages (paid extracts)
protections: A Woningborg or SWK guarantee covering completion if the builder fails, and a warranty after handover
Payments in instalments tied to construction stages
A retention of part of the price at handover until snags are resolved
Transfer by notarial deed
checks: The guarantee certificate for this home
The instalment schedule and the expected handover date
The owners' association (VvE) budget and reserve
Ground lease (erfpacht) terms, if any
Insolvency notices for the builder

PT.name: Portugal
sources: The commercial register: the developer company and its officers
Citius: insolvency and court proceedings
The municipality (Câmara Municipal): building licence and licence of use
The land registry (registo predial) and the tax register (caderneta predial): owner and encumbrances
The housing technical file (ficha técnica da habitação)
protections: A promissory contract (CPCV) with a deposit: by law, if the seller defaults the buyer may claim double the deposit
A deed needs a valid licence of use for the home
checks: The building licence and the licence of use
Encumbrances in the land registry
The deposit and default terms of the promissory contract
The condominium title and its charges
Court and insolvency records for the developer

IT.name: Italy
sources: The company register (Registro Imprese): the developer, its officers and filings
Court records: insolvency and disputes
The municipality: the building permit (permesso di costruire) and certificate of habitability
The land and mortgage registers (Catasto, Conservatoria): paid extracts
protections: Legislative Decree 122/2005: off-plan buyers receive a bank or insurance guarantee (fideiussione) for sums paid, and a ten-year building insurance policy
The preliminary contract for a home under construction must be made before a notary
checks: The guarantee (fideiussione) covering every payment
The ten-year insurance policy
The building permit and habitability certificate
Mortgages and liens on the land
The developer's insolvency and court record

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
sources: The Wafi off-plan sales programme: whether the project is licensed and its escrow account
The Real Estate General Authority (REGA)
The Ministry of Commerce: the developer's commercial registration
Najiz (Ministry of Justice): property deeds and court services
Tadawul disclosures when the developer is listed
protections: Off-plan sales must be licensed under Wafi, with buyer payments into an escrow account
checks: The Wafi licence number and its scope
The escrow account and how payments are released
The commercial registration of the seller
The completion date and delay terms
The title deed on handover

ZA.name: South Africa
sources: The NHBRC: whether the builder is registered and the home is enrolled
The companies register (CIPC): the developer, its directors and status
The Deeds Office: title and bonds
The municipality: approved building plans and the occupancy certificate
protections: The Housing Consumers Protection Measures Act: builders must be NHBRC-registered and enrol each new home
The NHBRC warranty for major structural defects
Sectional title schemes: levies and the body corporate's finances
checks: The NHBRC registration and enrolment certificate
How the deposit is held (in trust) and when it is released
Occupation and transfer dates
Levies and the reserve fund
The developer's company status

BR.name: Brazil
sources: The property registry (Registro de Imóveis): the registered incorporation (memorial de incorporação) and liens
The company register (CNPJ, Receita Federal)
State courts (TJ) and Jusbrasil: disputes involving the developer
The municipality: building permit and occupancy certificate (habite-se)
protections: Law 4.591/1964: a development must be registered before units are sold
Ring-fencing of the project's assets (patrimônio de afetação) where the developer has elected it
Law 13.786/2018: rules for cancelling a purchase and a 180-day tolerance on delivery
checks: The registered incorporation for this project
Whether the project is ring-fenced
The delivery date and the tolerance clause
Cancellation (distrato) terms
Lawsuits against the developer

MX.name: Mexico
sources: The public property registry of the state: title and liens
The municipality: construction licence and land-use permits
PROFECO: the developer's registered sales contract
The company register (Registro Público de Comercio)
protections: NOM-247-SE-2021: information and contract rules for selling new homes
Foreigners in the restricted zone near coasts and borders buy through a bank trust (fideicomiso)
checks: Clear title and permits for the land
The bank trust, for a foreign buyer in the restricted zone
How deposits are held and the delivery date
The condominium regime and fees
The developer's track record and lawsuits

JP.name: Japan
sources: The national search of licensed real estate businesses and construction businesses: the seller's licence and any administrative actions
The legal affairs bureau's property and company registers (paid extracts)
The municipality: building confirmation and completion inspection
protections: The Building Lots and Buildings Transaction Business Act: protection of deposits on off-plan sales, and the important-matters explanation before contract
The Housing Quality Assurance Act: ten years' liability for structural defects, backed by insurance or a deposit
checks: The licence number and any administrative actions
The deposit protection for this sale
The building confirmation and completion inspection
Management fees and the repair reserve
Earthquake-resistance standards met

TH.name: Thailand
sources: The Department of Business Development (DBD): the developer company
The Land Department: title deed and encumbrances
Condominium registration
The environmental impact assessment approval for larger projects
Stock Exchange of Thailand disclosures when the developer is listed
protections: The Condominium Act: the foreign ownership quota for each building
Standard terms for condominium sale contracts
checks: Whether the foreign quota allows the purchase
The EIA approval and building permit
The title deed and any mortgage over the project
Juristic person fees and the sinking fund
Transfer fees and who pays them

PH.name: Philippines
sources: DHSUD: the project's certificate of registration and licence to sell
The SEC: the developer company
The Registry of Deeds: title and encumbrances
Court records
protections: Presidential Decree 957: projects must be registered and licensed before units are sold
The Maceda Law (Republic Act 6552): refund rights for buyers paying in instalments who cancel
checks: The licence to sell for this project and phase
Title and encumbrances on the land
The completion date and the developer's obligations
Refund terms on cancellation
Association dues
